Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Consolidating Aurora renewal redlines / plan to sign

Team —

Quick summary: Aurora is ready to move but legal pulled a few last items that would block e-sign. I pulled Neha's initial notes and Ben's pricing change request into a single packet (see attachments). Goal: get to a single consolidated redline and a DocuSign path by 12/10.

High-level asks: 
- Neha: can you lead legal consolidation and call out anything we can't concede?
- Ben: confirm final capacity numbers and whether the 12% uplift you proposed is locked for this renewal.
- Marcus: ops acceptance on the SLA language/credits and any data-retention constraints.
- Lauren: be ready to queue for Finance for the invoice schedule.

Attached: Aurora_MSA_v3_redline.pdf (Neha's markup), Aurora_OrderForm_consolidated_v1.docx (pricing + capacity table), pricing-summary-uptick.xlsx

Proposed next steps (timeline):
1) Internal consolidate by 11/15
2) Send consolidated redline to Aurora legal for confirmation 11/16
3) Quick sync with Aurora procurement 11/19 if needed; otherwise, DocuSign week of 12/6

If anyone sees a fatal term that will push this beyond 12/10, flag immediately.

Thanks —
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0184

--- Attachment stubs: Aurora_OrderForm_consolidated_v1.docx (docx), Aurora_MSA_v3_redline.pdf (pdf)
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Consolidating Aurora renewal redlines / plan to sign

Thanks, Mateo. I reviewed Aurora's submitted changes and annotated the attached MSA. High-level legal positions: 

- Term & auto-renew: Aurora is asking to move from 12 to 18 months and remove the auto-renew clause. We're OK with 18 months if they accept the uplift pricing and notify 60 days before expiry.
- Data deletion / export: they want a permanent export window of 180 days; ops (Marcus) needs to confirm feasibility for long-term retention for pager logs.
- SLA credits: legal wants an explicit SLA credit table. Ops suggested we keep existing credit caps but add a single-percent ramp for severe outages beyond month 3. I flagged language where we cannot accept unlimited credits.
- Indemnity & Security: external counsel asked to add narrow carveouts for third-party infra; propose language in section 7.

I'm attaching a redline PDF (Aurora_MSA_v3_redline.pdf). I can consolidate into a single tracked Word if that helps.

Action items for me: produce a consolidated MSA with in-line comments by 11/15. If anyone has non-negotiable asks, call them out by EOD 11/12.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Head of Contracts | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai

--- Attachment stub: Aurora_MSA_v3_redline.pdf (pdf)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 08:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Consolidating Aurora renewal redlines / plan to sign

Adding a quick pricing note: Aurora verbally agreed to the 12% volume uplift for committed capacity, but procurement is pushing to keep price per token flat and ask for an additional 3% credit if usage exceeds committed for two consecutive months. I recommend we: 

- Keep the committed rate at the proposed uplift (12%) for the 18-month term.
- Offer a temporary usage credit (one-time) for first-month overage during migration to the new capacity rather than an ongoing multi-month credit.

Marcus — can you confirm whether we can support a one-time migration overage credit and still preserve forecasted utilization?

Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

Date: Tue, 16 Nov 2026 10:00:00 -0800
Subject: Aurora renewal — consolidated redline and sign-off options

Jordan / Mariya —

Thanks again for the productive conversations last week. Attached is our consolidated packet that combines Aurora's requested edits and our internal responses: Aurora_MSA_v3_redline.pdf and Aurora_OrderForm_consolidated_v1.docx. Neha called out the remaining items where we need Aurora confirmation (term length, SLA credit cap, and data-export window). Ben has also included the agreed capacity uplift and a proposed single migration overage credit.

Two paths to finish this quickly: 

Option A (fast): Aurora accepts the consolidated redline as-is with the 18-month term + single migration credit. We upload to DocuSign and aim for signatures by 12/10. DocuSign link will be sent once Aurora OKs.

Option B (sync): If you prefer to walk through the three outstanding items, let's schedule a 30-minute call this week. Below are proposed times: Wed 11/18 9:00–9:30 PT, Thu 11/19 11:00–11:30 PT.

Please reply with which option you prefer and any last edits. If you choose Option A, we will route to Finance for invoice sequencing and send the DocuSign link.

Regards,
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Aurora renewal — consolidated redline and sign-off options

Mateo —

Thanks for consolidating. We prefer Option B and would like a quick sync to confirm three small items: 

1) Term: Aurora legal will accept 18 months if the auto-renew remains but with a 60-day notice window (they prefer to keep the renewal safety net).
2) Data export: can you confirm that logs and KV snapshots are exportable for 180 days and that we can get a one-time bulk export at term end?
3) SLA credits: we want the first-month overage credit converted to a recurring two-month protection during the migration period only.

Can we do Wed 11/24 10:00–10:30 PT? If that works, Mariya will prepare our redline notes and I will circulate a short agenda.

Jordan Ellison
Director, Cloud Platform | AuroraData
j.ellison@auroradata.com
